title: Telemetry Gatekeeper for function-call / structured-output shape compatibility during rollouts
creator: Alyssa Cheng
description: Problem: During canary and A/B rollouts we see silent regressions in function-call signatures and structured output shapes that only surface in production after significant traffic has been routed. Existing guards detect diffs but are noisy and slow to attribute root cause per-customer. Goal: implement a lightweight "Telemetry Gatekeeper" service that evaluates shape compatibility and functional contract deltas in real time for rollouts, drives automated rollbacks when defined risk thresholds are exceeded, and powers per-customer rollback granularity and postmortem telemetry.
acceptance_criteria: Gatekeeper computes a per-request schema-compatibility score (0.0-1.0) for function calls and structured outputs and emits it to tracing/metrics
Support canary policies that define: minimum pass-rate, max-severity threshold, sampling window, and per-customer weight adjustments
Automated rollback trigger that can mark canaries as failed and reduce traffic to baseline model within 30s of threshold breach (configurable)
Dashboards with 90th/99th percentile compatibility score and example diffs for failed requests
Low CPU overhead: gatekeeper adds <3ms median latency on p95 path in the serving runtime (measured at 8k RPS test)
Security review completed and KMS keys used for sensitive telemetry scrubbed before storage
design_decisions: Run Gatekeeper as a lightweight sidecar in the serving runtime to preserve per-request context and avoid sampling mismatch between runtime and telemetry
Use a hybrid comparator: deterministic canonical schema equality check plus fuzzy similarity (field-level Levenshtein/nesting score) to surface non-breaking but risky changes
Emit structured diffs to a shadow sink at 1% sample for full payload archival; only metadata and hashed pointers stored for high-volume paths
Expose an API for rollout rules: canary policies tied to model version tags, customer-id overrides, and time-based ramp schedules
Use conservative defaults: require 99% pass-rate for function-call signatures and 95% for optional structured fields during first 24h of a canary
implementation_notes: Proto: gatekeeper accepts (request_id, model_version, customer_id, function_name, predicted_shape, expected_shape) and returns compatibility_score + diff_summary
Shape representation: canonical JSON Schema derived from model's function-call spec and best-effort inference for free-form JSON outputs using field path heuristics
Performance: cache compiled schemas per-model-version and warm on rollout start; use lock-free LRU for compiled schema cache
Backpressure: if gatekeeper CPU exceeds threshold, degrade to sampling mode and emit a metric 'gatekeeper.degraded'

updates: 2026-02-12: Spike results - fuzzy comparator prototype achieves 0.91 precision / 0.87 recall vs our labeled diffs set; median extra latency 1.8ms on microbenchmark (8k RPS). Logged PR: github.com/redwood-inference/gatekeeper/pull/12

2026-02-18: Design review with PM and SRE. Decision: sidecar approach accepted; we will also expose a lightweight library for Dedicated/private where sidecar isn't feasible. Action: add per-customer rollback in scope.

2026-02-24: Marco implemented compiled-schema cache and lock-free LRU; integration tests show p95 latency increase under load is 2.9ms. Uploaded benchmark dashboard: https://grafana.redwood.company/d/rollouts/gatekeeper-benchmarks
2026-03-02: Security review kickoff: identified need to hash PII in telemetry before archival. Security ask: use envelope encryption via KMS. Ticket: SEC-1294
2026-03-07: PM feedback: require an 'explain' endpoint to return human-readable diff examples for Console investigation. Added to acceptance criteria.
2026-03-10: Canary policy schema finalized: {min_pass_rate, max_severity, window_sec, sample_pct, per_customer_overrides}. Policy API proto: github.com/redwood-inference/rollouts/pull/45

2026-03-12: Integration test - simulated A/B with new Gatekeeper: one failing change produced 6.3% failed compatibility score and automated rollback triggered after 3-window breaches. Follow-up: reduce default window from 5m to 2m for faster feedback in high-traffic apps. Recording: runbook/gatekeeper-rollback-2026-03-12.md
risks_and_mitigations: False positives on fuzzy comparator could cause unnecessary rollbacks -> mitigation: require severity aggregation and at least 3 breach windows before auto-rollback for global rollouts; immediate per-customer rollback only if failure rate for that customer is >50%
Telemetry volume when archiving full diffs -> mitigation: 1% full payload shadow sink, rest only metadata and hashed pointers
Late-binding schemas for free-form outputs may misclassify benign changes -> mitigation: add developer opt-out markers for known unstable endpoints
telemetry_queries: SELECT model_version, count(*) as total, sum(case when compatibility_score < 0.8 then 1 else 0 end) as failures, pctile(compatibility_score, 0.99) as p99_score FROM gatekeeper.events WHERE time > now() - interval '30 minutes' GROUP BY model_version ORDER BY failures DESC LIMIT 50;

SELECT customer_id, model_version, count(*) AS requests, sum(case when compat_diff_severity = 'high' then 1 else 0 end) AS high_sev FROM gatekeeper.events WHERE time > now() - interval '1 hour' GROUP BY customer_id, model_version HAVING high_sev > 10 ORDER BY high_sev DESC LIMIT 100;
-- Alert rule: trigger when failures / total > 0.02 for >2 windows of 2 minutes each

-- Example quickcheck: fetch 10 failing examples for model_version X: SELECT example_id, diff_summary FROM gatekeeper.examples WHERE model_version = 'v2026-03-10' AND compatibility_score < 0.8 ORDER BY time DESC LIMIT 10;
